name: churn-model runtime: kserve-lgbserver modelFormat: lightgbm storageUri: s3://models/churn/v2 serviceAccountName: s3-sa ``` Storage credentials are described in [S3 and air-gapped](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/examples/air-gapped-and-s3/). ## Runtime and format pairs | Runtime | `modelFormat` | Artifact | --- | --- | --- | `kserve-sklearnserver` | `sklearn` | `model.joblib` or `model.pkl` | `kserve-xgbserver` | `xgboost` | `model.bst` or `model.json` | `kserve-lgbserver` | `lightgbm` | `model.txt` or `model.bst` | `kserve-pmmlserver` | `pmml` | `model.pmml` | `kserve-paddleserver` | `paddle` | Paddle inference model | `kserve-autogluonserver` | `autogluon` | AutoGluon predictor directory | `kserve-mlserver` | `sklearn`, `xgboost`, `lightgbm`, `mlflow` | MLServer layout | `kserve-tensorflow-serving` | `tensorflow` | SavedModel directory | `kserve-torchserve` | `pytorch` | `.mar` archive | Confirm formats against the live cluster: ```sh kubectl get clusterservingruntime kserve-sklearnserver -o jsonpath='{.spec.supportedModelFormats}' ``` ## scikit-learn Export with joblib: ```python import joblib joblib.dump(pipeline, "model.joblib") ``` Upload so the artifact sits directly under the URI prefix: ``` s3://models/fraud/v3/model.joblib ``` ```yaml models: - name: fraud-detector runtime: kserve-sklearnserver modelFormat: sklearn storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3 ``` ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/fraud-detector:predict \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"instances": [[5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2], [6.2, 2.9, 4.3, 1.3]]}' ``` ## XGBoost ```python model.save_model("model.bst") ``` ```yaml models: - name: demand-forecast runtime: kserve-xgbserver modelFormat: xgboost storageUri: s3://models/demand/v7 ``` ## LightGBM ```python model.save_model("model.txt") ``` ```yaml models: - name: churn-model runtime: kserve-lgbserver modelFormat: lightgbm storageUri: s3://models/churn/v2 ``` ## PMML Useful for models exported from R, SAS, or legacy toolchains: ```yaml models: - name: credit-score runtime: kserve-pmmlserver modelFormat: pmml storageUri: s3://models/credit/v1 ``` ## PyTorch with TorchServe Package with `torch-model-archiver`, then: ```yaml models: - name: image-classifier runtime: kserve-torchserve modelFormat: pytorch storageUri: s3://models/vision/resnet resources: requests: cpu: "2" memory: 4Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi ``` ## TensorFlow Point at the directory containing the version folder: ```yaml models: - name: recommender runtime: kserve-tensorflow-serving modelFormat: tensorflow storageUri: s3://models/recommender/v2 ``` ## MLServer One runtime for several frameworks, including MLflow models: ```yaml models: - name: mlflow-model runtime: kserve-mlserver modelFormat: mlflow storageUri: s3://models/mlflow/run-42 ``` ## Resource sizing Classic models are small. Over-requesting wastes capacity: ```yaml resources: requests: cpu: "500m" memory: 1Gi limits: cpu: "2" memory: 2Gi ``` Raise limits for large ensembles and wide feature sets. ## Disabling unused runtimes Fewer runtimes means fewer cluster-scoped objects: ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: enabled: true huggingfaceserver: disabled: true huggingfaceserver_multinode: disabled: true vllmserver: disabled: true tritonserver: disabled: true torchserve: disabled: true paddleserver: disabled: true autogluonserver: disabled: true ``` ## Verify ```sh kubectl get inferenceservice -n models kubectl port-forward -n models svc/fraud-detector-predictor 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/fraud-detector curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/fraud-detector:predict \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"instances": [[5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2]]}' ``` | Problem | Fix | --- | --- | `No such file or directory: model.joblib` | Artifact not at the URI root; check the object path | Version mismatch on load | Match the training library version to the runtime image | `NoSupportingRuntime` | Set `runtime` and `modelFormat` explicitly |

52.title: Disaggregated prefill
52.content: # Disaggregated prefill Prefill processes the prompt and is compute-bound. Decode generates tokens and is memory-bandwidth-bound. Splitting them lets each pool scale and be sized independently. Use it for long prompts, retrieval-augmented generation, and workloads where prompt length varies widely. ## Complete values file ```yaml namespace: models hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret llmDefaults: image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct name: llama-3.1-8b-instruct # Decode pool args: - --model - /mnt/models - --served-model-name - llama-3.1-8b-instruct - --enforce-eager replicas: 2 resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" # Prefill pool. Unset fields fall back to the decode pool above. prefill: replicas: 2 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --enable-chunked-prefill - --max-num-batched-tokens - "8192" resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 64Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "2" ``` `HF_TOKEN` is injected into the prefill containers automatically, exactly as it is for the decode pool. ## Minimal form When both pools share the same image and arguments, an empty `prefill` is enough: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" prefill: {} ``` ## Sizing the two pools | Phase | Bound by | Favors | --- | --- | --- | Prefill | Compute | Fewer, larger GPUs; high batch token limits | Decode | Memory bandwidth and capacity | More replicas; large key-value cache | Starting points: | Traffic | Prefill | Decode | --- | --- | --- | Long prompts, short answers | Larger pool | Smaller pool | Short prompts, long answers | Smaller pool | Larger pool | Retrieval-augmented generation | 2 x 2 GPUs | 2–4 x 1 GPU | ## Different hardware per pool Put prefill on the faster accelerator: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" prefill: replicas: 2 nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-h100 priorityClassName: prefill-priority args: - --model - /mnt/models - --enable-chunked-prefill resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "2" ``` The decode pool lands on A100 nodes and prefill on H100 nodes. The prefill pool inherits the toleration because it does not define one. ## Combining with multi-node decode ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "4" resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 128Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "4" parallelism: tensor: 4 data: 8 dataLocal: 4 worker: {} prefill: replicas: 1 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "4" - --enable-chunked-prefill ``` The prefill pool inherits the image, resources, and placement from the decode pool, so only the differing arguments are listed. ## Multi-node prefill Spread the prefill pool across nodes with `prefill.worker`, mirroring the decode pool: ```yaml prefill: parallelism: tensor: 4 data: 8 dataLocal: 4 worker: {} ``` Give prefill workers their own placement when needed: ```yaml prefill: worker: nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 priorityClassName: prefill-worker ``` ## Useful arguments | Argument | Pool | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | `--enable-chunked-prefill` | Prefill | Splits long prompts into chunks | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | Prefill | Token budget per batch | `--enforce-eager` | Decode | Lower memory, no CUDA graphs | `--max-num-seqs` | Decode | Concurrent sequence cap | ## Is it worth it? Disaggregation adds moving parts and total GPU cost. Start with the simpler layout in [vLLM on GPU](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/examples/vllm-gpu-llm/) and adopt this only when measurements justify it: - Time-to-first-token is dominated by long prompts. - Prefill and decode utilization are clearly unbalanced. - You have enough GPUs for two separate pools. ## Verify ```sh kubectl get llminferenceservice llama-8b-disagg -n models kubectl get pods -n models -o wide kubectl logs -n models -l app.kubernetes.io/name=llama-8b-disagg --tail=100 ``` Measure time-to-first-token with a long prompt: ```sh kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b-disagg 8080:80 time curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "llama-3.1-8b-instruct", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the following: ..."}], "max_tokens": 64 }' > /dev/null ```

53.title: Gated and private models
53.content: # Gated and private models Llama, Gemma, Mistral, and private organization repositories all require a Hugging Face token. ## Preparing access 1. Sign in to Hugging Face and open the model page, for example `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`. 2. Accept the license and wait for approval; some models approve instantly, others take hours. 3. Create a **read** token at . 4. Verify access before deploying: ```sh export HF_TOKEN="hf_replace_me" curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \ https://huggingface.co/api/models/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ``` `200` means access is granted. `401` means the token is wrong, `403` means the license is not accepted for that account. ## Externally managed Secret The recommended pattern: the chart references the Secret but never stores the token. ```sh kubectl create namespace models kubectl create secret generic hf-secret \ --namespace models \ --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN" ``` ```yaml namespace: models hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` ## Chart-managed Secret Simpler for development. Never commit the token. ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: true managed: true name: hf-secret token: "" ``` ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve --create-namespace \ -f values.yaml \ --set-string hfSecret.token="$HF_TOKEN" ``` > [!CAUTION] > A token passed this way is stored in the Helm release Secret. Anyone able to read Secrets in the release namespace can recover it. ## Gated model examples ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" - name: gemma-9b model: uri: hf://google/gemma-2-9b-it resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" - name: mistral-7b model: uri: hf://mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` CPU variants through the `models` list: ```yaml models: - name: vllm-gemma-3-4b runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://google/gemma-3-4b-it args: - --served-model-name - gemma-3-4b-it ``` ## Private organization repositories Identical mechanism; the token must belong to a member with read access. ```yaml models: - name: internal-classifier runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://my-org/internal-classifier args: - --task=sequence_classification ``` ## Different tokens per workload Disable automatic injection and set the variable explicitly: ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret models: - name: shared-model storageUri: hf://my-org/shared-model - name: restricted-model storageUri: hf://restricted-org/private-model injectHfToken: false env: - name: HF_TOKEN valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: restricted-org-token key: HF_TOKEN ``` ```sh kubectl create secret generic restricted-org-token \ -n models --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$RESTRICTED_TOKEN" ``` ## Prefill pools Prefill containers receive the token automatically, so a disaggregated workload needs no extra configuration: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" prefill: replicas: 2 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "2" ``` If you supply `containers` explicitly under `prefill.template`, that definition is used verbatim and you provide the environment variable yourself. ## Multiple namespaces The Secret must exist in every namespace that runs a workload: ```sh for ns in models team-a team-b; do kubectl create secret generic hf-secret -n "$ns" --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN" done ``` ## Avoiding repeated gated downloads Mirror the model once into storage you control, then deploy from there. See [S3 and air-gapped](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/examples/air-gapped-and-s3/) and [Local model cache](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/local-model-cache/). Check the model license before redistributing weights internally. ## Troubleshooting ```sh kubectl logs -n models -c storage-initializer --tail=50 kubectl get secret hf-secret -n models ``` | Message | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | `401 Unauthorized` | Token missing or invalid | Recreate the Secret with a valid token | `403 Forbidden` | License not accepted | Accept it with the account owning the token | `404 Not Found` | Wrong repository, or private with no access | Check the path and permissions | `CreateContainerConfigError` | Secret missing in this namespace | Create it in the workload namespace | Token works locally, not in cluster | Wrong namespace or key name | Key must be `HF_TOKEN` |

54.title: Hugging Face runtime
54.content: # Hugging Face runtime `kserve-huggingfaceserver` serves transformer models for classification, token classification, embeddings, fill-mask, and text generation, on CPU or GPU. ## Complete values file ```yaml namespace: models hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: enabled: true huggingfaceserver: disabled: false enabled: true modelDefaults: runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface resources: requests: cpu: "2" memory: 8Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 16Gi models: - name: sentiment storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english args: - --task=sequence_classification ``` ## Tasks The runtime usually infers the task, but setting it explicitly avoids surprises. | Task | Argument | Example model | --- | --- | --- | Sequence classification | `--task=sequence_classification` | `distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english` | Token classification | `--task=token_classification` | `dslim/bert-base-NER` | Fill mask | `--task=fill_mask` | `bert-base-uncased` | Text embedding | `--task=text_embedding` | `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | Text generation | `--task=text_generation` | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` | ## Embeddings Common for retrieval and vector search: ```yaml models: - name: embeddings runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 args: - --task=text_embedding resources: requests: cpu: "2" memory: 4Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi ``` ```sh kubectl port-forward -n models svc/embeddings-predictor 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/openai/v1/embeddings \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "embeddings", "input": ["first sentence", "second sentence"]}' ``` Larger, higher-quality embedding models: ```yaml - name: embeddings-large storageUri: hf://BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 args: - --task=text_embedding resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi limits: cpu: "8" memory: 16Gi ``` ## Named entity recognition ```yaml models: - name: ner storageUri: hf://dslim/bert-base-NER args: - --task=token_classification ``` ## Text generation with GPU The runtime can use the vLLM backend when a GPU is present: ```yaml models: - name: llama-1b runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct args: - --task=text_generation - --backend=vllm - --max-model-len=4096 resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: 16Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Force the pure transformers backend on CPU: ```yaml args: - --task=text_generation - --backend=huggingface ``` ## Multiple tasks together ```yaml models: - name: sentiment storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english args: [--task=sequence_classification] - name: ner storageUri: hf://dslim/bert-base-NER args: [--task=token_classification] - name: embeddings storageUri: hf://sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 args: [--task=text_embedding] - name: fill-mask storageUri: hf://bert-base-uncased args: [--task=fill_mask] ``` ## Multi-node variant `kserve-huggingfaceserver-multinode` serves very large transformer models across nodes: ```yaml models: - name: large-transformer runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver-multinode modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct resources: requests: cpu: "16" memory: 128Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "4" limits: cpu: "16" memory: 128Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "4" ``` For most large generative workloads, prefer [Multi-node LLM](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/examples/multi-node-llm/). ## Calling the model Classification through the KServe protocol: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/sentiment:predict \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"instances": ["This release is excellent", "This is disappointing"]}' ``` Open Inference Protocol: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/v2/models/sentiment/infer \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"inputs": [{"name": "input-0", "shape": [1], "datatype": "BYTES", "data": ["great product"]}]}' ``` ## Tuning | Setting | Purpose | --- | --- | `--max-model-len` | Context limit for generation | `--backend` | `vllm` or `huggingface` | `--dtype` | Precision selection | `OMP_NUM_THREADS` | CPU thread count | `--tensor-input-names` | Custom input naming | ```yaml env: - name: OMP_NUM_THREADS value: "4" - name: TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE value: "1" ```

55.title: Multi-node LLM
55.content: # Multi-node LLM For models that do not fit on the GPUs of a single node. Adding a `worker` key enables LeaderWorkerSet-based serving. ## Prerequisites ```sh kubectl get crd leaderworkersets.leaderworkerset.x-k8s.io kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.'nvidia\.com/gpu' ``` Multi-node serving requires fast node-to-node networking. Without RDMA or high-bandwidth interconnect, throughput suffers badly. ## Complete values file Two nodes with four GPUs each, tensor parallel four. ```yaml namespace: models hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret llmDefaults: image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct name: llama-3.1-70b-instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --served-model-name - llama-3.1-70b-instruct - --tensor-parallel-size - "4" - --max-model-len - "8192" - --dtype - bfloat16 resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 128Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "4" parallelism: tensor: 4 data: 8 dataLocal: 4 worker: {} ``` ## Parallelism keys | Key | Meaning | --- | --- | `tensor` | GPUs splitting each layer; usually the per-node GPU count | `pipeline` | Stages splitting layers across groups | `data` | Total GPUs across the deployment | `dataLocal` | GPUs per node | Node count is `data / dataLocal`. Above, `8 / 4` gives two nodes. > [!IMPORTANT] > `parallelism.tensor` and `--tensor-parallel-size` must agree with the GPU limit per pod. Mismatches cause startup failures or silent under-use. ## Sizing examples | Model | dtype | Total GPU memory | Layout | --- | --- | --- | --- | 70B | bfloat16 | ~140 GB plus cache | 2 nodes x 4 x 40 GB | 70B | bfloat16 | ~140 GB plus cache | 1 node x 8 x 80 GB | 405B | bfloat16 | ~810 GB plus cache | 4 nodes x 8 x 80 GB | 405B | FP8 | ~405 GB plus cache | 2 nodes x 8 x 80 GB | Single node with eight GPUs, no worker needed: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b-single-node model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "8" resources: limits: cpu: "32" memory: 256Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "8" ``` ## Very large models Four nodes with eight GPUs each, combining tensor and pipeline parallelism: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-405b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "8" - --pipeline-parallel-size - "4" - --max-model-len - "4096" resources: limits: cpu: "64" memory: 512Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "8" parallelism: tensor: 8 pipeline: 4 data: 32 dataLocal: 8 worker: {} ``` ## Different worker shape Workers reuse the leader definition unless overridden: ```yaml worker: image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "4" resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 128Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "4" ``` ## Placing leader and worker on different hardware Both pods accept scheduling fields. A worker inherits the leader's placement unless it sets its own: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-h100 tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule parallelism: tensor: 4 data: 8 dataLocal: 4 worker: nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 priorityClassName: worker-priority ``` Here the leader lands on an H100 node, workers on A100 nodes, and the worker inherits the toleration because it does not define one. See [GPU and scheduling](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/gpu-and-scheduling/). ## Shared memory Multi-node vLLM is sensitive to `/dev/shm` size. If you see `Bus error` or NCCL failures, raise it through an `LLMInferenceServiceConfig` referenced with `baseRefs`, or use a runtime that already sets a larger value. ## Cold starts A 70B model is roughly 140 GB of weights. Downloading that on every pod start is slow and expensive. Strongly consider: - [Local model cache](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/local-model-cache/) for node-local copies - A `pvc://` source shared across pods - An in-region object storage mirror ## Verify ```sh kubectl get llminferenceservice llama-70b -n models kubectl get leaderworkerset -n models kubectl get pods -n models -o wide ``` Leader and worker pods should be spread across nodes. Check GPU use on each: ```sh kubectl exec -n models -- nvidia-smi kubectl exec -n models -- nvidia-smi ``` Then test: ```sh kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-70b 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "llama-3.1-70b-instruct", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain tensor parallelism."}], "max_tokens": 256 }' ``` ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | Workers never become ready | LeaderWorkerSet controller missing | Install the controller | NCCL timeout | Network too slow or blocked | Check interconnect and network policy | Only leader uses GPUs | Parallelism mismatch | Align `parallelism` with vLLM arguments | Pods pending | Not enough whole nodes free | Free capacity or reduce `data` | Out of memory at load | Context too large | Lower `--max-model-len` |

56.title: OpenVINO on CPU
56.content: # OpenVINO on CPU The OpenVINO Model Server gives efficient CPU inference for OpenVINO IR, ONNX, and TensorFlow models, and can also run small text-generation models. It is the chart default for `modelDefaults.runtime`. ## Complete values file ```yaml namespace: models clusterServingRuntimes: openVINO: enabled: true name: kserve-openvino image: openvino/model_server:2026.3 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: requests: cpu: "2" memory: 4Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi vllmCPU: enabled: false modelDefaults: runtime: kserve-openvino modelFormat: huggingface resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: 16Gi limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi models: - name: ovms-gemma-3-4b storageUri: hf://OpenVINO/gemma-3-4b-it-fp16-ov args: - --task=text_generation - --target_device=CPU - --log_level=INFO - --cache_size=2 ``` Install: ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve --create-namespace -f openvino-values.yaml ``` ## Pre-converted models Models under the `OpenVINO` organization on Hugging Face are already converted to OpenVINO IR and load fastest. ```yaml models: - name: ovms-gemma-4-e2b storageUri: hf://OpenVINO/gemma-4-E2B-it-fp16-ov args: - --task=text_generation - --target_device=CPU - name: ovms-gemma-4-e4b storageUri: hf://OpenVINO/gemma-4-E4B-it-fp16-ov args: - --task=text_generation - --target_device=CPU ``` ## ONNX models ```yaml models: - name: resnet-onnx runtime: kserve-openvino modelFormat: onnx storageUri: s3://models/vision/resnet50 resources: requests: cpu: "2" memory: 4Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi ``` ## TensorFlow models ```yaml models: - name: recommender-tf runtime: kserve-openvino modelFormat: tensorflow storageUri: s3://models/recommender/v2 ``` ## Useful arguments | Argument | Purpose | --- | --- | `--task=text_generation` | Selects the generation pipeline | `--target_device=CPU` | Execution device; `AUTO` and `GPU` also exist | `--cache_size=2` | Key-value cache size in GB for generation | `--log_level=DEBUG` | Verbose logs while diagnosing | `--nireq=4` | Number of concurrent inference requests | ## Performance notes CPU inference scales with physical cores. Give the pod whole cores and keep requests equal to limits for predictable latency: ```yaml resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi ``` Pin thread counts when the node is shared: ```yaml env: - name: OMP_NUM_THREADS value: "8" ``` ## Verify ```sh kubectl get inferenceservice -n models kubectl port-forward -n models svc/ovms-gemma-3-4b-predictor 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/openai/v1/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "ovms-gemma-3-4b", "prompt": "Kubernetes is", "max_tokens": 64}' ``` For a classification or vision model: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/resnet-onnx:predict \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"instances": [[[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]]]}' ```

57.title: Triton and ONNX
57.content: # Triton and ONNX NVIDIA Triton Inference Server runs TensorRT, ONNX, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and Python backends, with GPU support and dynamic batching. For CPU-only ONNX, OpenVINO is usually lighter. ## Complete values file ```yaml namespace: models kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: enabled: true tritonserver: disabled: false image: nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver tag: 23.05-py3 models: - name: resnet-triton runtime: kserve-tritonserver modelFormat: onnx storageUri: s3://models/vision/resnet50 serviceAccountName: s3-sa resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "8" memory: 16Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` ## Repository layout Triton expects a model repository, not a bare file: ``` s3://models/vision/ └── resnet50/ ├── config.pbtxt └── 1/ └── model.onnx ``` `config.pbtxt`: ``` name: "resnet50" platform: "onnxruntime_onnx" max_batch_size: 8 input [ { name: "input" data_type: TYPE_FP32 dims: [ 3, 224, 224 ] } ] output [ { name: "output" data_type: TYPE_FP32 dims: [ 1000 ] } ] ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > Point `storageUri` at the directory **containing** the model folder, not at the version directory. ## Dynamic batching Improves throughput for bursty traffic: ``` dynamic_batching { preferred_batch_size: [ 4, 8 ] max_queue_delay_microseconds: 10000 } ``` ## TensorRT Fastest on NVIDIA GPUs, but engines are built for a specific GPU and TensorRT version: ``` name: "resnet50_trt" platform: "tensorrt_plan" max_batch_size: 8 ``` ```yaml models: - name: resnet-trt runtime: kserve-tritonserver modelFormat: tensorrt storageUri: s3://models/vision/resnet50_trt resources: requests: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` ## CPU-only ONNX Triton runs ONNX on CPU, but OpenVINO is usually more efficient: ```yaml models: - name: resnet-openvino runtime: kserve-openvino modelFormat: onnx storageUri: s3://models/vision/resnet50 resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi limits: cpu: "8" memory: 16Gi ``` ## Several models on one server Triton loads every model in the repository: ``` s3://models/production/ ├── resnet50/ │ ├── config.pbtxt │ └── 1/model.onnx ├── bert_qa/ │ ├── config.pbtxt │ └── 1/model.onnx └── yolo/ ├── config.pbtxt └── 1/model.plan ``` ```yaml models: - name: vision-suite runtime: kserve-tritonserver modelFormat: onnx storageUri: s3://models/production resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 16Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "16" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Address each by name through the V2 protocol. ## Calling Triton ```sh kubectl port-forward -n models svc/resnet-triton-predictor 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/v2/models/resnet50 curl -s http://localhost:8080/v2/health/ready curl -s http://localhost:8080/v2/models/resnet50/infer \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "inputs": [ { "name": "input", "shape": [1, 3, 224, 224], "datatype": "FP32", "data": [0.0] } ] }' ``` ## Mirroring the image `nvcr.io` may be unreachable in restricted clusters: ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: tritonserver: image: registry.example.com/mirror/tritonserver tag: 23.05-py3 imagePullSecrets: - name: registry-credentials ``` ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | `failed to load model` | Bad repository layout | Verify `config.pbtxt` and the numeric version directory | `unsupported platform` | Wrong `platform` value | Match it to the artifact type | `model not found` in requests | Wrong name in URL | Use the name from `config.pbtxt` | TensorRT engine fails | Built for another GPU or version | Rebuild on the target GPU | Image pull failure | `nvcr.io` blocked | Mirror the image | ```sh kubectl logs -n models -l serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice=resnet-triton -c kserve-container --tail=100 ```

58.title: vLLM on CPU
58.content: # vLLM on CPU Runs generative models without a GPU. Use it for development, integration tests, and small models. > [!WARNING] > CPU generation is slow. Expect seconds per token for multi-billion-parameter models. Do not use this for production chat traffic. ## Complete values file ```yaml namespace: models hfSecret: enabled: true managed: true token: "" clusterServingRuntimes: vllmCPU: enabled: true name: kserve-vllm-cpu image: public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-cpu-release-repo:v0.26.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent maxModelLen: 4096 gpuMemoryUtilization: "0.7" shmSize: 2Gi openVINO: enabled: true models: - name: vllm-gemma-3-4b runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://google/gemma-3-4b-it args: - --served-model-name - gemma-3-4b-it resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi limits: cpu: "8" memory: 48Gi ``` Install with the token supplied at the command line: ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve --create-namespace \ -f vllm-cpu-values.yaml \ --set-string hfSecret.token="$HF_TOKEN" ``` Gemma is a gated model. See [Gated and private models](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/examples/gated-and-private-models/). ## Several models side by side ```yaml models: - name: vllm-gemma-3-4b runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://google/gemma-3-4b-it args: - --served-model-name - gemma-3-4b-it - name: vllm-gemma-4-e4b runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://google/gemma-4-E4B-it args: - --served-model-name - gemma-4-E4B-it - name: vllm-gemma-4-e2b runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://google/gemma-4-E2B-it args: - --served-model-name - gemma-4-E2B-it ``` Each entry is a separate deployment with its own memory footprint. Size the node accordingly. ## Small ungated models No token required, and quick to start: ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: false models: - name: tinyllama runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 args: - --served-model-name - tinyllama - --dtype - float32 resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 16Gi ``` ## Tuning for CPU | Setting | Effect | --- | --- | `maxModelLen` | Lower values cut memory use substantially | `shmSize` | Raise if vLLM reports shared memory errors | `--dtype float32` | Often required; CPUs may lack bfloat16 support | `OMP_NUM_THREADS` | Match to allocated CPU for stable throughput | ```yaml clusterServingRuntimes: vllmCPU: maxModelLen: 2048 shmSize: 4Gi models: - name: vllm-small runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 env: - name: OMP_NUM_THREADS value: "8" - name: VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE value: "4" ``` ## Memory guidance Allow roughly: model weights, plus key-value cache, plus about 4 GB overhead. | Model | dtype | Suggested memory limit | --- | --- | --- | 1.1B | float32 | 16 GB | 3–4B | bfloat16 | 32–48 GB | 7–8B | bfloat16 | 64 GB | An `OOMKilled` pod needs a higher limit or a lower `maxModelLen`. ## Verify ```sh kubectl get inferenceservice -n models kubectl logs -n models -l serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice=vllm-gemma-3-4b -c kserve-container --tail=50 kubectl port-forward -n models svc/vllm-gemma-3-4b-predictor 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/openai/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "gemma-3-4b-it", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], "max_tokens": 32 }' ``` The first request after startup is slower because the engine warms up.

59.title: vLLM on GPU
59.content: # vLLM on GPU Standard single-node LLM serving with an OpenAI-compatible API. This is the usual production starting point. ## Complete values file ```yaml namespace: models hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret components: llmisvcCrd: enabled: true llmisvc: enabled: true llmDefaults: replicas: 1 image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 args: - --model - /mnt/models resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct name: llama-3.1-8b-instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --served-model-name - llama-3.1-8b-instruct - --max-model-len - "8192" - --dtype - bfloat16 - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.90" replicas: 2 resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Create the token Secret, then install: ```sh kubectl create namespace models kubectl create secret generic hf-secret -n models --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN" helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve --create-namespace -f gpu-values.yaml ``` ## Serving several models ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --max-model-len - "8192" resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" - name: mistral-7b model: uri: hf://mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --max-model-len - "16384" resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" - name: qwen-14b model: uri: hf://Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "2" - --max-model-len - "8192" resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 64Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "2" ``` ## Quantized models Quantization fits larger models on smaller GPUs at some quality cost. ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b-awq model: uri: hf://hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --quantization - awq - --tensor-parallel-size - "2" - --max-model-len - "4096" resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 96Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "2" ``` ## Common vLLM arguments | Argument | Purpose | --- | --- | `--served-model-name` | Name clients pass in the `model` field | `--max-model-len` | Context window; the strongest memory lever | `--gpu-memory-utilization` | Fraction of GPU memory to use, typically `0.85`–`0.95` | `--tensor-parallel-size` | GPUs per replica; must equal the GPU limit | `--dtype` | `bfloat16`, `float16`, or `auto` | `--quantization` | `awq`, `gptq`, `fp8` | `--enable-chunked-prefill` | Improves throughput with long prompts | `--max-num-seqs` | Concurrent sequence cap | `--enforce-eager` | Disables CUDA graphs; lowers memory, reduces speed | ## Alternative: the models list For a simple single-node deployment, the classic list also works and uses the upstream runtime: ```yaml models: - name: llama-8b-isvc runtime: kserve-vllmserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 4 scaleMetric: concurrency scaleTarget: 80 resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "8" memory: 48Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` The `models` list renders scheduling and scaling fields directly, which `llmInferenceServices` does not. Choose `llmInferenceServices` when you need routing, multi-node, disaggregation, or LLM-aware autoscaling. ## Verify ```sh kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models kubectl get pods -n models -w kubectl logs -n models -l app.kubernetes.io/name=llama-8b --tail=100 kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "llama-3.1-8b-instruct", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a haiku about storage."}], "max_tokens": 128, "temperature": 0.7 }' ``` Watch GPU use: ```sh kubectl exec -n models deploy/llama-8b -- nvidia-smi ```

60.title: GPU and scheduling
60.content: # GPU and scheduling ## Requesting GPUs GPUs are requested like any other extended resource. Requests and limits must match. `models` entry: ```yaml models: - name: llama-gpu runtime: kserve-vllmserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "8" memory: 48Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` `llmInferenceServices` entry: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-gpu model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Common resource keys: | Vendor | Resource key | --- | --- | NVIDIA | `nvidia.com/gpu` | AMD | `amd.com/gpu` | Intel | `gpu.intel.com/i915` | AWS Neuron | `aws.amazon.com/neuron` | Confirm what your nodes advertise: ```sh kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.'nvidia\.com/gpu' ``` ## Sizing GPU memory Rough guide for weights only; add headroom for the key-value cache, activations, and the CUDA context. | Parameters | FP16 / BF16 | 8-bit | 4-bit | --- | --- | --- | --- | 1B | ~2 GB | ~1 GB | ~0.5 GB | 7–8B | ~16 GB | ~8 GB | ~4 GB | 13B | ~26 GB | ~13 GB | ~7 GB | 70B | ~140 GB | ~70 GB | ~35 GB | An 8B model in BF16 fits on a single 24 GB GPU with a modest context. A 70B model needs multiple GPUs; see [Multi-node LLM](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/examples/multi-node-llm/). Control cache usage with vLLM arguments: ```yaml args: - --model - /mnt/models - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.90" - --max-model-len - "8192" ``` > [!TIP] > If a pod fails with a CUDA out-of-memory error at startup, lower `--max-model-len` first, then `--gpu-memory-utilization`. ## Node placement ### Resource-based scheduling Requesting `nvidia.com/gpu` already restricts a pod to GPU nodes. If your GPU nodes carry no taints, no further configuration is needed. ### Placement for `models` entries `models` entries render placement fields directly. Set them per model, or once in `modelDefaults`. ```yaml models: - name: llama-gpu runtime: kserve-vllmserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct nodeSelector: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: g5.2xlarge tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "8" memory: 48Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Apply the same placement to every model: ```yaml modelDefaults: nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule ``` Node affinity for finer control, such as pinning to a zone: ```yaml models: - name: llama-gpu storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct affinity: nodeAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeSelectorTerms: - matchExpressions: - key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone operator: In values: [eu-west-1a, eu-west-1b] podAntiAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: - weight: 100 podAffinityTerm: topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname labelSelector: matchLabels: serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice: llama-gpu ``` Spread replicas evenly: ```yaml topologySpreadConstraints: - maxSkew: 1 topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule labelSelector: matchLabels: serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice: llama-gpu ``` Other supported placement fields are `priorityClassName`, `schedulerName`, and `nodeName`. > [!NOTE] > A per-model value replaces the `modelDefaults` value rather than merging with it. Repeat any entries you still need. ### Placement through a custom runtime Still useful when many models share a placement profile and you would rather not repeat it. Runtime-level settings apply to every model using that runtime: ```yaml apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: ClusterServingRuntime metadata: name: vllm-gpu-tainted spec: supportedModelFormats: - name: huggingface autoSelect: false containers: - name: kserve-container image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 args: - --model=/mnt/models nodeSelector: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: g5.2xlarge tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule ``` A value set on the `models` entry takes precedence over the runtime. ### Placement for LLM workloads `llmInferenceServices` entries render placement fields into the leader pod, and into the worker pod when multi-node serving is enabled. ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule priorityClassName: high-priority runtimeClassName: nvidia resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Apply the same placement to every LLM workload: ```yaml llmDefaults: nodeSelector: pool: gpu tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule ``` Supported pod fields are `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, `affinity`, `topologySpreadConstraints`, `priorityClassName`, `schedulerName`, `nodeName`, `runtimeClassName`, `serviceAccountName`, `imagePullSecrets`, `volumes`, `initContainers`, `securityContext`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, `automountServiceAccountToken`, `hostIPC`, `hostNetwork`, `shareProcessNamespace`, `restartPolicy`, `dnsPolicy`, `dnsConfig`, and `hostAliases`. #### Worker placement A worker inherits the leader's placement. Override any field under `worker` to split the two pools across different hardware: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-h100 parallelism: tensor: 4 data: 8 dataLocal: 4 worker: nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 priorityClassName: worker-priority ``` Resolution order for a worker field is `worker` → entry → `llmDefaults`. The first level that sets the key wins, and the value replaces rather than merges. #### Shared placement profiles An `LLMInferenceServiceConfig` still works when several workloads share one profile: ```yaml apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: LLMInferenceServiceConfig metadata: name: gpu-placement namespace: models spec: template: nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule ``` ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct baseRefs: - gpu-placement ``` #### Prefill placement A prefill pool inherits the workload's placement and accepts the same fields, so the two pools can sit on different hardware: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 prefill: replicas: 2 nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-h100 priorityClassName: prefill-priority ``` `prefill.worker` takes the same fields for multi-node prefill. ### Cluster-wide defaults For tainted GPU fleets, a cluster administrator can apply default tolerations with an admission controller or a mutating policy, so every GPU pod tolerates the taint without per-workload configuration. ## Controller placement Controller pods accept placement through the dependency roots: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: controller: nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/os: linux tolerations: - key: control-plane operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule affinity: {} topologySpreadConstraints: [] ``` ## Multi-GPU on one node Request several GPUs and set tensor parallelism to match: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b-single-node model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "8" resources: limits: cpu: "32" memory: 256Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "8" ``` `--tensor-parallel-size` must equal the GPU count in `limits`. ## Shared memory vLLM uses `/dev/shm` for inter-process communication. The Kubernetes default of 64 MB is too small. For the chart's CPU runtime: ```yaml clusterServingRuntimes: vllmCPU: shmSize: 2Gi ``` For upstream runtimes: ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: vllmserver: devShm: enabled: true sizeLimit: 8Gi ``` A `Bus error` or a shared-memory failure in the logs usually means this value is too small. ## Diagnosing scheduling failures ```sh kubectl get pods -n models kubectl describe pod -n models | sed -n '/Events/,$p' kubectl describe node ``` | Message | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` | No free GPUs | Free capacity, add nodes, or lower the request | `node(s) had untolerated taint` | GPU nodes are tainted | Add `tolerations` to the model entry or `modelDefaults` | `0/N nodes are available` | No node matches the selector | Verify labels with `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` | Pod `Pending` with no events | Cluster autoscaler still provisioning | Watch the autoscaler logs |

61.title: Hugging Face
61.content: # Hugging Face How to pull models from Hugging Face, including public, gated, and private repositories. ## The `hf://` URI ```yaml models: - name: sentiment runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english ``` The format is `hf://{organization}/{repository}`. The storage initializer downloads the repository and mounts it at `/mnt/models` before the runtime starts. Pin a revision when the runtime supports it: ```yaml storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct:refs%2Fpr%2F1 ``` > [!TIP] > Public models need no token. Configure credentials only for gated or private repositories, or to avoid anonymous rate limits. ## Token configuration ### Chart-managed Secret The chart creates the Secret from the token you supply. ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: true managed: true name: hf-secret token: "hf_replace_me" ``` Never commit the token. Pass it at install time: ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve \ -f values.yaml \ --set-string hfSecret.token="$HF_TOKEN" ``` Or keep it in a separate, protected file: ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve -f values.yaml -f secrets.yaml ``` ### Externally managed Secret Preferred with sealed secrets, External Secrets Operator, or Vault. The chart injects the reference but does not create the Secret. ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret ``` Create the Secret in the **workload** namespace, with the key `HF_TOKEN`: ```sh kubectl create secret generic hf-secret \ --namespace models \ --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN" ``` > [!CAUTION] > The key must be exactly `HF_TOKEN`. A Secret with a different key renders successfully but the pod fails to start with a missing key error. ## How the token reaches the pod When `hfSecret.enabled` is `true`, the chart adds this to each generated `models` entry and to the leader and worker containers of `llmInferenceServices`: ```yaml env: - name: HF_TOKEN valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: hf-secret key: HF_TOKEN ``` Opt out for a specific workload: ```yaml models: - name: public-model storageUri: hf://sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 injectHfToken: false ``` Prefill pools receive the token on the same terms as the leader. Disable it for the prefill pool alone: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct prefill: replicas: 2 injectHfToken: false ``` > [!NOTE] > Supplying `containers` explicitly under `template`, `worker`, or `prefill.template` replaces the generated container, so that pool receives only the `env` you define there. ## Gated models Models such as Llama and Gemma require accepting a license first. 1. Sign in to Hugging Face and open the model page. 2. Accept the license and wait for approval. 3. Create a token with **read** access at . 4. Confirm the token can see the repository: ```sh curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \ https://huggingface.co/api/models/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | head ``` A `401` or `403` means the token lacks access; the download will fail the same way inside the cluster. ## Private repositories Private repositories use the same token mechanism. Ensure the token belongs to a user or organization with access: ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret models: - name: internal-model runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://my-org/internal-classifier ``` ## Multiple tokens The chart injects a single Secret reference. For workloads needing different tokens, disable injection and set the variable explicitly. ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret models: - name: team-a-model storageUri: hf://team-a/model injectHfToken: false env: - name: HF_TOKEN valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: team-a-hf-token key: HF_TOKEN ``` ## Offline and mirrored environments Point the client at an internal mirror: ```yaml models: - name: mirrored-model runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://my-org/model env: - name: HF_ENDPOINT value: https://hf-mirror.internal.example.com ``` Prevent any network call once the artifact is mounted: ```yaml env: - name: TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE value: "1" - name: HF_HUB_OFFLINE value: "1" ``` For clusters with no internet access, copy models to object storage and use `s3://`. See [S3 and air-gapped](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/examples/air-gapped-and-s3/). ## Reducing repeated downloads Every pod restart re-downloads the model unless it is cached. Options: - Enable node-local caching. See [Local model cache](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/local-model-cache/). - Copy the model into a PVC and use `pvc://`. See [Storage URIs](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/storage-uris/). - Mirror the model into object storage close to the cluster. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid token | Verify the Secret exists in the workload namespace with key `HF_TOKEN` | `403 Forbidden` | Gated license not accepted | Accept the license with the account owning the token | `404 Not Found` | Wrong repository name or private without access | Check the `hf://org/repo` path | Pod stuck `Init:0/1` | Download still running | Watch `kubectl logs -c storage-initializer -n models` | `CreateContainerConfigError` | Secret or key missing | `kubectl get secret hf-secret -n models -o jsonpath='{.data}'` | Inspect the download directly: ```sh kubectl logs -n models -c storage-initializer ```

62.title: Inference services
62.content: # Inference services The `models` list renders one `InferenceService` per entry. Use it for predictive models and for single-container generative models that do not need multi-node serving. ## Fields | Field | Required | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | --- | `name` | Yes | — | Resource name and part of the endpoint URL | `storageUri` | Yes | — | Model artifact location. See [Storage URIs](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/storage-uris/) | `runtime` | No | `modelDefaults.runtime` | ClusterServingRuntime name | `modelFormat` | No | `modelDefaults.modelFormat` | Format advertised by the runtime | `args` | No | `modelDefaults.args` | Extra container arguments | `env` | No | `modelDefaults.env` | Extra environment variables | `resources` | No | `modelDefaults.resources` | CPU, memory, and GPU requests and limits | `volumeMounts` | No | `modelDefaults.volumeMounts` | Mounts for the model container | `namespace` | No | `namespace` | Per-model namespace override | `serviceAccountName` | No | `serviceAccount.name` | ServiceAccount for the predictor pod | `injectHfToken` | No | `true` | Set `false` to skip `HF_TOKEN` injection | ### Scheduling fields | Field | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | `nodeSelector` | `modelDefaults.nodeSelector` | Restrict the pod to matching nodes | `tolerations` | `modelDefaults.tolerations` | Tolerate node taints | `affinity` | `modelDefaults.affinity` | Node and pod affinity rules | `topologySpreadConstraints` | `modelDefaults.topologySpreadConstraints` | Spread replicas across a topology | `priorityClassName` | `modelDefaults.priorityClassName` | Scheduling priority | `schedulerName` | `modelDefaults.schedulerName` | Alternative scheduler | `nodeName` | `modelDefaults.nodeName` | Pin to one node; bypasses the scheduler | ### Scaling fields | Field | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | `minReplicas` | `modelDefaults.minReplicas` | Lower bound; `0` enables scale to zero | `maxReplicas` | `modelDefaults.maxReplicas` | Upper bound | `scaleTarget` | `modelDefaults.scaleTarget` | Target value for the chosen metric | `scaleMetric` | `modelDefaults.scaleMetric` | `concurrency`, `rps`, `cpu`, or `memory` | `containerConcurrency` | `modelDefaults.containerConcurrency` | Concurrent requests per replica | `timeout` | `modelDefaults.timeout` | Request timeout in seconds | `canaryTrafficPercent` | `modelDefaults.canaryTrafficPercent` | Traffic share for a new revision | `deploymentStrategy` | `modelDefaults.deploymentStrategy` | Rollout strategy | ### Pod metadata and other fields | Field | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | `labels` | `modelDefaults.labels` | Labels applied to the predictor pod | `annotations` | `modelDefaults.annotations` | Annotations applied to the predictor pod | `imagePullSecrets` | `modelDefaults.imagePullSecrets` | Registry credentials | `volumes` | `modelDefaults.volumes` | Pod volumes, paired with `volumeMounts` | > [!NOTE] > A per-model value replaces the `modelDefaults` value; maps and lists are not merged. Fields set in neither place are omitted so KServe applies its own defaults. `minReplicas: 0` is honoured rather than treated as unset. ## Rendered shape This entry: ```yaml models: - name: sentiment runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english ``` renders: ```yaml apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1 kind: InferenceService metadata: name: sentiment namespace: models spec: predictor: serviceAccountName: hf-sa model: runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: name: huggingface storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi limits: cpu: "8" memory: 48Gi ``` ## Defaults `modelDefaults` applies to every entry that omits a field. Defaults are replaced, never merged: an entry that sets `resources` must set all the limits and requests it needs. ```yaml modelDefaults: runtime: kserve-openvino modelFormat: huggingface args: [] env: [] resources: requests: cpu: "4" memory: 16Gi limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi ``` ## Multiple models Each entry is independent and can mix runtimes, formats, and storage backends. ```yaml models: - name: fraud-sklearn runtime: kserve-sklearnserver modelFormat: sklearn storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3 resources: requests: cpu: "1" memory: 2Gi limits: cpu: "2" memory: 4Gi - name: demand-xgboost runtime: kserve-xgbserver modelFormat: xgboost storageUri: s3://models/demand/v7 resources: requests: cpu: "1" memory: 2Gi limits: cpu: "2" memory: 4Gi - name: embeddings runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 args: - --task=text_embedding resources: requests: cpu: "2" memory: 8Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 16Gi ``` ## Passing runtime arguments `args` are appended to the runtime container. Valid arguments depend on the runtime. OpenVINO: ```yaml models: - name: ovms-gemma runtime: kserve-openvino modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://OpenVINO/gemma-3-4b-it-fp16-ov args: - --task=text_generation - --target_device=CPU - --log_level=DEBUG - --cache_size=2 ``` vLLM on CPU: ```yaml models: - name: vllm-gemma runtime: kserve-vllm-cpu modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://google/gemma-3-4b-it args: - --served-model-name - gemma-3-4b-it - --dtype - bfloat16 ``` Hugging Face runtime: ```yaml models: - name: classifier runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english args: - --task=sequence_classification - --backend=huggingface ``` ## Environment variables `env` accepts standard Kubernetes environment entries, including references to Secrets and ConfigMaps. ```yaml models: - name: tuned-model storageUri: s3://models/tuned/v2 env: - name: OMP_NUM_THREADS value: "8" - name: TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE value: "1" - name: CUSTOM_API_KEY valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: model-credentials key: api-key ``` When `hfSecret.enabled` is `true`, `HF_TOKEN` is injected first and your `env` entries follow. ## GPU models Request GPUs in `resources`: ```yaml models: - name: llama-gpu runtime: kserve-vllmserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "8" memory: 48Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` GPU requests and limits must be equal; Kubernetes does not overcommit GPUs. ## Scheduling onto specific nodes ```yaml models: - name: llama-gpu runtime: kserve-vllmserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 tolerations: - key: nvidia.com/gpu operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule priorityClassName: high-priority resources: requests: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" limits: cpu: "8" memory: 48Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Spread replicas across nodes and zones: ```yaml topologySpreadConstraints: - maxSkew: 1 topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway labelSelector: matchLabels: serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice: llama-gpu ``` See [GPU and scheduling](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/gpu-and-scheduling/) for sizing and diagnosis. ## Scaling a model ```yaml models: - name: sentiment runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english minReplicas: 2 maxReplicas: 8 scaleMetric: concurrency scaleTarget: 80 containerConcurrency: 4 timeout: 120 ``` Scale to zero between requests: ```yaml - name: batch-scorer storageUri: s3://models/batch/v1 minReplicas: 0 maxReplicas: 4 ``` See [Autoscaling](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/autoscaling/). ## Pod labels, annotations, and volumes ```yaml models: - name: scratch-model storageUri: s3://models/large/v1 labels: tier: production annotations: prometheus.io/scrape: "true" volumes: - name: scratch emptyDir: sizeLimit: 16Gi volumeMounts: - name: scratch mountPath: /scratch ``` `labels` and `annotations` apply to the predictor pod. `volumes` belongs to the pod and `volumeMounts` to the model container, so they are normally set together. ## Shared defaults for every model ```yaml modelDefaults: runtime: kserve-openvino modelFormat: huggingface nodeSelector: pool: inference tolerations: - key: dedicated operator: Equal value: inference effect: NoSchedule minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 4 models: - name: inherits-everything storageUri: s3://models/a/v1 - name: overrides-placement storageUri: s3://models/b/v1 nodeSelector: pool: gpu minReplicas: 2 ``` ## Per-model namespaces ```yaml namespace: models models: - name: shared-model storageUri: s3://models/shared/v1 - name: team-a-model namespace: team-a storageUri: s3://models/team-a/v1 serviceAccountName: team-a-sa ``` > [!CAUTION] > The chart creates the ServiceAccount only in `namespace`. A model deployed to another namespace needs a ServiceAccount that already exists there, and a copy of any referenced Secret such as `hf-secret`. ## Verifying ```sh kubectl get inferenceservice -n models kubectl describe inferenceservice sentiment -n models kubectl get pods -n models kubectl logs -n models -l serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice=sentiment -c kserve-container ``` `READY` becomes `True` when the model has downloaded and the runtime reports healthy. First start includes the download, which can take several minutes for large models. ## Calling the model ```sh kubectl port-forward -n models svc/sentiment-predictor 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/sentiment:predict \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"instances": ["This product is excellent"]}' ``` Generative runtimes expose OpenAI-compatible paths: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/openai/v1/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "vllm-gemma", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 64}' ``` See [Networking and endpoints](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/networking-and-endpoints/) for ingress access.

63.title: Installation
63.content: # Installation ## Prerequisites | Requirement | Detail | --- | --- | Kubernetes | 1.30 or later | Helm | 3.19 or later | cert-manager | Required by the KServe controller webhooks | Gateway API CRDs | Required when you use Gateway-based routing or `LLMInferenceService` routers | GPU device plugin | Required for any GPU workload, for example the NVIDIA device plugin | LeaderWorkerSet | Required only for multi-node `LLMInferenceService` workloads | Check cert-manager before installing: ```sh kubectl get pods -n cert-manager kubectl get crd certificates.cert-manager.io ``` ## Namespaces This chart uses two distinct namespaces. | Namespace | Purpose | Controlled by | --- | --- | --- | Release namespace | KServe controllers, webhooks, and shared configuration | `helm --namespace` | Workload namespace | Your `InferenceService` and `LLMInferenceService` objects | `namespace` value | Install the controllers into `kserve`. KServe `v0.20.0` contains namespace-sensitive webhook and cert-manager references, so a different release namespace is not supported. ```yaml # values.yaml namespace: models ``` ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve --create-namespace \ -f values.yaml ``` Create the workload namespace yourself; the chart does not create it: ```sh kubectl create namespace models ``` ## Install from source ```sh helm dependency build helm-charts/model-serving helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve --create-namespace \ -f my-values.yaml ``` `helm dependency build` downloads the seven pinned KServe charts listed in `Chart.lock`. Run it after every clone and after any dependency change. ## Install from the registry ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving \ oci://ghcr.io/sassoftware/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/model-serving \ --version 0.1.0 \ --namespace kserve --create-namespace \ -f my-values.yaml ``` Published chart versions are immutable. Pin `--version` in every environment. ## Verify the installation ```sh helm status model-serving -n kserve kubectl get pods -n kserve kubectl get clusterservingruntime kubectl get inferenceservice -n models kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models ``` A healthy controller namespace shows running `kserve-controller-manager` and, when enabled, `llmisvc-controller-manager` pods. ## Preview the rendered manifests Always review before applying to a shared cluster: ```sh helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve --include-crds -f my-values.yaml > rendered.yaml ``` ## Upgrade ```sh helm dependency build helm-charts/model-serving helm upgrade model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve -f my-values.yaml ``` Adding or removing entries in `models` and `llmInferenceServices` is a normal upgrade. Removing an entry deletes the corresponding workload. ## Uninstall ```sh helm uninstall model-serving -n kserve ``` > [!CAUTION] > Helm does not delete CRDs on uninstall. Custom resources such as `InferenceService` remain registered cluster-wide. Deleting the CRDs deletes every model object in every namespace. To remove the CRDs deliberately: ```sh kubectl get crd | grep kserve.io kubectl delete crd inferenceservices.serving.kserve.io ``` ## CRD lifecycle and existing KServe installations Helm applies subchart CRDs before templates. If KServe is already installed by another release or by `kubectl apply`, the cluster-scoped CRDs, webhooks, and cluster roles already have an owner and this install will conflict. Before installing into such a cluster: 1. List existing owners: `helm list -A | grep -i kserve`. 2. Remove the previous installation, or disable the overlapping components with `components.*.enabled: false`. 3. Confirm no leftover webhooks remain: `kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration | grep kserve`. See [Components](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/components/) for selectively disabling parts of KServe.

64.title: LLM inference services
64.content: # LLM inference services The `llmInferenceServices` list renders one `LLMInferenceService` per entry. Use it for generative models that need multi-node serving, disaggregated prefill and decode, LLM-aware routing, or request-driven autoscaling. Unlike `models`, these entries do not use a ClusterServingRuntime. You define the container image and arguments directly. ## Fields | Field | Required | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | --- | `name` | Yes | — | Resource name | `model` | Yes | — | Model block; `model.uri` is required | `image` | No | `llmDefaults.image` | Container image for leader and worker | `args` | No | `llmDefaults.args` | Container arguments | `resources` | No | `llmDefaults.resources` | Requests and limits | `replicas` | No | `llmDefaults.replicas` | Fixed replica count; ignored when `scaling` is set | `parallelism` | No | — | Tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism | `worker` | No | — | **Presence** enables multi-node serving | `prefill` | No | — | **Presence** enables a separate prefill pool | `router` | No | `llmDefaults.router` | Gateway, route, and scheduler configuration | `scaling` | No | — | Autoscaling configuration; replaces `replicas` | `baseRefs` | No | — | `LLMInferenceServiceConfig` references to compose | `volumeMounts` | No | `llmDefaults.volumeMounts` | Mounts for the main container | `labels` | No | `llmDefaults.labels` | Labels on the workload | `annotations` | No | `llmDefaults.annotations` | Annotations on the workload | `namespace` | No | `namespace` | Namespace override | `injectHfToken` | No | `true` | Set `false` to skip `HF_TOKEN` injection | ### Pod fields These render into the leader pod, and into the worker pod when `worker` is present. Each can also be set once in `llmDefaults`. | Group | Fields | --- | --- | Scheduling | `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, `affinity`, `topologySpreadConstraints`, `priorityClassName`, `schedulerName`, `nodeName` | Identity | `serviceAccountName`, `automountServiceAccountToken`, `imagePullSecrets` | Runtime | `runtimeClassName`, `securityContext`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, `restartPolicy` | Storage | `volumes`, paired with `volumeMounts` on the container | Networking | `hostNetwork`, `hostIPC`, `shareProcessNamespace`, `dnsPolicy`, `dnsConfig`, `hostAliases` | Init | `initContainers` | > [!NOTE] > A value set on an entry replaces the `llmDefaults` value rather than merging with it. Fields set in neither place are omitted so KServe applies its own default. `false` and `0` are honoured rather than treated as unset. ## Minimal example ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` This uses `llmDefaults.image` (`vllm/vllm-openai:latest`) and `llmDefaults.args` (`--model /mnt/models`). ## The model block `model` is passed through unchanged, so any field the CRD supports is available. ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct name: llama-3.1-8b-instruct ``` `model.name` is the identifier clients send in the OpenAI-style `model` field. It defaults to the resource name. ## Defaults ```yaml llmDefaults: replicas: 1 image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest args: [--model, /mnt/models] resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 64Gi router: gateway: {} route: {} scheduler: {} ``` > [!TIP] > Pin the image in production. `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` changes without notice. ```yaml llmDefaults: image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 ``` The model is mounted at `/mnt/models`, so `--model /mnt/models` is correct for vLLM. Keep that argument when you override `args`. ## Single-node GPU serving ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --served-model-name - llama-3.1-8b - --max-model-len - "8192" - --dtype - bfloat16 replicas: 2 resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` ## Multi-node serving Adding a `worker` key enables multi-node serving through LeaderWorkerSet. An empty map reuses the leader image, arguments, and resources. ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-70b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "4" resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 128Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "4" parallelism: tensor: 4 data: 8 dataLocal: 4 worker: {} ``` `data` divided by `dataLocal` determines the node count. Above, `8 / 4` gives two nodes with four GPUs each. Give workers a different shape when needed: ```yaml worker: image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --tensor-parallel-size - "4" resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 128Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "4" ``` Workers also accept the pod fields listed above, which is how you place leader and worker on different hardware: ```yaml nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-h100 worker: nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 priorityClassName: worker-priority ``` A worker field resolves in the order `worker` → entry → `llmDefaults`, so a worker that sets nothing inherits the leader's placement. > [!IMPORTANT] > `worker: {}` and omitting `worker` are different. An empty map still enables multi-node serving. Multi-node serving requires the LeaderWorkerSet controller: ```sh kubectl get crd leaderworkersets.leaderworkerset.x-k8s.io ``` ## Disaggregated prefill and decode Separate the compute-bound prefill phase from the memory-bound decode phase. Adding a `prefill` key enables the pool, exactly like `worker`. The simplest form reuses the workload's image, arguments, resources, and placement: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" prefill: {} ``` Tune and place the prefill pool independently by setting fields inside `prefill`: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b-disagg model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct args: - --model - /mnt/models - --enforce-eager nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-a100 resources: limits: cpu: "8" memory: 32Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "1" prefill: replicas: 2 args: - --model - /mnt/models - --enable-chunked-prefill nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-h100 resources: limits: cpu: "16" memory: 64Gi nvidia.com/gpu: "2" ``` `prefill` accepts the same container keys as the workload (`image`, `args`, `resources`, `volumeMounts`, `injectHfToken`), the same pod fields, and its own `replicas`, `parallelism`, `scaling`, `labels`, and `annotations`. Anything unset falls back to the workload, then to `llmDefaults`. `HF_TOKEN` is injected into the prefill containers on the same terms as the leader. Disable it for the prefill pool alone with `prefill.injectHfToken: false`. ### Multi-node prefill Adding `prefill.worker` spreads the prefill pool across nodes, mirroring the top-level `worker`: ```yaml prefill: parallelism: tensor: 4 data: 8 dataLocal: 4 worker: {} ``` ### Full control over the prefill container Supplying `containers` under `prefill.template` replaces the generated container and is passed through verbatim, including any `env` you set: ```yaml prefill: replicas: 2 template: nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-h100 containers: - name: main image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 args: [--model, /mnt/models, --enable-chunked-prefill] env: - name: HF_TOKEN valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: hf-secret key: HF_TOKEN ``` The same escape hatch exists for the leader and worker through `template.containers` and `worker.containers`. ## Routing The default router requests a managed gateway, route, and scheduler: ```yaml llmDefaults: router: gateway: {} route: {} scheduler: {} ``` Attach to an existing gateway, or disable parts of the router: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct router: gateway: refs: - name: shared-gateway namespace: infrastructure route: {} scheduler: {} ``` See [Networking and endpoints](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/networking-and-endpoints/). ## Autoscaling Setting `scaling` removes the fixed `replicas` field from the rendered resource. ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct scaling: minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 8 ``` See [Autoscaling](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/autoscaling/). ## Composing shared configuration `baseRefs` references `LLMInferenceServiceConfig` objects, letting several workloads share a base definition. ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct baseRefs: - standard-gpu-profile ``` Enable the shipped configs when you use this pattern: ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: llmisvcConfigs: enabled: true ``` ## Verifying ```sh kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models kubectl describe llminferenceservice llama-8b -n models kubectl get pods -n models -w kubectl logs -n models -l app.kubernetes.io/name=llama-8b --tail=100 ``` ## Calling the model ```sh kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b 8080:80 curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "llama-8b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize Kubernetes in one sentence."}], "max_tokens": 128 }' ```

65.title: Local model cache
65.content: # Local model cache Node-local caching stores model weights on node disks so pods skip the download on every start. It is the main remedy for slow cold starts with large models. ## When to use it | Situation | Benefit | --- | --- | Multi-gigabyte LLMs | Removes repeated multi-minute downloads | Scale-to-zero workloads | Greatly reduces cold-start time | Frequent rollouts | Restarts reuse cached weights | Metered egress | Downloads the model once per node, not once per pod | Skip it for small models, or when a `pvc://` shared volume already serves the same purpose. ## Enabling The controller ships disabled. Enable the components and the controller: ```yaml components: localModelCrd: enabled: true localModel: enabled: true kserve-localmodel-resources: kserve: localmodel: enabled: true jobNamespace: kserve-localmodel-jobs jobTTLSecondsAfterFinished: 3600 agent: hostPath: /mnt/models ``` Create the job namespace before installing: ```sh kubectl create namespace kserve-localmodel-jobs ``` Apply the change: ```sh helm upgrade model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -n kserve -f values.yaml kubectl get pods -n kserve | grep localmodel ``` ## Node groups A node group defines where cached models live and which nodes participate. ```yaml apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: LocalModelNodeGroup metadata: name: gpu-cache spec: persistentVolumeSpec: accessModes: - ReadWriteOnce capacity: storage: 500Gi hostPath: path: /mnt/models type: DirectoryOrCreate persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Delete storageClassName: standard persistentVolumeClaimSpec: accessModes: - ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 500Gi storageClassName: standard storageLimit: 400Gi ``` Label the nodes that should cache models: ```sh kubectl label node gpu-node-1 kserve/localmodel=worker ``` The agent daemonset selector is configurable: ```yaml kserve-localmodel-resources: kserve: localmodelnode: controller: nodeSelector: kserve/localmodel: worker ``` ## Caching a model ```yaml apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: LocalModelCache metadata: name: llama-8b-cache spec: sourceModelUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct modelSize: 20Gi nodeGroups: - gpu-cache ``` The controller runs download jobs and reports progress: ```sh kubectl get localmodelcache kubectl describe localmodelcache llama-8b-cache kubectl get jobs -n kserve-localmodel-jobs kubectl get localmodelnode ``` Gated models need credentials available to the download job; use the same token Secret described in [Hugging Face](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/huggingface/). ## Using a cached model Reference the same URI as usual. When the cache covers that URI on the scheduled node, the pod uses the local copy. ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" ``` Verify by comparing pod start time with and without the cache: ```sh kubectl get events -n models --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -20 ``` ## Namespace scope `LocalModelNamespaceCache` restricts which namespaces may use a cached model: ```yaml apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: LocalModelNamespaceCache metadata: name: llama-8b-models spec: localModelCache: llama-8b-cache namespace: models ``` ## Capacity planning Cached models consume node disk permanently.
