Size `storageLimit` for the sum of every cached model plus headroom, and monitor: ```sh kubectl describe localmodelnode kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,DISK:.status.allocatable.ephemeral-storage ``` Remove a cached model by deleting its `LocalModelCache`: ```sh kubectl delete localmodelcache llama-8b-cache ``` ## Volume management Disable the controller's volume handling if your platform provisions node volumes itself: ```yaml kserve-localmodel-resources: kserve: localmodel: disableVolumeManagement: true ``` ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Check | --- | --- | Download job never starts | Does `jobNamespace` exist? Is the controller running? | Job fails on a gated model | Token Secret present in the job namespace | Pods still download the model | Node labeled and part of the node group | Node disk full | Lower `storageLimit` or delete unused caches | Agent pods missing | Node selector does not match any node | ```sh kubectl logs -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-localmodel-controller-manager --tail=100 kubectl logs -n kserve-localmodel-jobs -l job-name= --tail=100 ```

66.title: Networking and endpoints
66.content: # Networking and endpoints ## Quick local access Port-forwarding needs no ingress and is the fastest way to verify a model. ```sh kubectl get svc -n models # Classic InferenceService kubectl port-forward -n models svc/sentiment-predictor 8080:80 # LLMInferenceService kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b 8080:80 ``` ## Endpoint paths | Workload | Path | Payload | --- | --- | --- | Predictive `InferenceService` | `/v1/models/{name}:predict` | `{"instances": [...]}` | Open Inference Protocol | `/v2/models/{name}/infer` | `{"inputs": [...]}` | Generative runtimes | `/openai/v1/completions` | OpenAI completion request | Generative runtimes | `/openai/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI chat request | `LLMInferenceService` | `/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI chat request | Predictive example: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/fraud-detector:predict \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"instances": [[5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2]]}' ``` Chat example: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "llama-8b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain vector databases briefly."}], "max_tokens": 200, "temperature": 0.2 }' ``` Streaming: ```sh curl -N http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "llama-8b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Count to ten"}], "stream": true}' ``` List served models: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models ``` ## In-cluster access Other workloads reach a model through the cluster service name: ``` http://sentiment-predictor.models.svc.cluster.local/v1/models/sentiment:predict http://llama-8b.models.svc.cluster.local/v1/chat/completions ``` Configure an OpenAI-compatible client with: ``` base_url = http://llama-8b.models.svc.cluster.local/v1 api_key = not-needed ``` ## Ingress for predictive workloads The core controller owns ingress defaults: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: controller: gateway: domain: models.example.com urlScheme: https ingressGateway: enableGatewayApi: true className: istio kserveGateway: kserve/kserve-ingress-gateway createGateway: false ``` With a domain configured, each model receives a hostname derived from the template: ``` https://sentiment-models.models.example.com ``` Adjust the pattern: {% raw %} ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: controller: gateway: domainTemplate: '{{ .Name }}-{{ .Namespace }}.{{ .IngressDomain }}' additionalIngressDomains: - internal.example.com ``` {% endraw %} For a non-Istio controller such as Contour, set the class name: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: controller: gateway: ingressGateway: className: contour ``` > [!WARNING] > A top-level `kserve:` block does not reach the subchart. Ingress settings must be under `kserve-resources`. Disable ingress creation entirely for internal-only clusters: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: controller: gateway: disableIngressCreation: true ``` ## Routers for LLM workloads `LLMInferenceService` uses a router with three parts: | Part | Purpose | --- | --- | `gateway` | Gateway API gateway that accepts traffic | `route` | HTTPRoute binding the gateway to the workload | `scheduler` | LLM-aware endpoint picker for cache- and load-aware routing | The chart default requests all three as managed: ```yaml llmDefaults: router: gateway: {} route: {} scheduler: {} ``` Attach to an existing gateway instead of creating one: ```yaml llmInferenceServices: - name: llama-8b model: uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct router: gateway: refs: - name: shared-gateway namespace: infrastructure route: {} scheduler: {} ``` Service-only exposure, with no gateway or route: ```yaml router: scheduler: {} ``` Several workloads can share one gateway by pointing at the same reference, which keeps a single external address and TLS certificate. ## Gateway API prerequisites ```sh kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io kubectl get gatewayclass kubectl get gateway -A kubectl get httproute -A ``` Install the Gateway API CRDs and a controller before enabling Gateway-based routing. ## TLS Terminate TLS at the gateway by referencing a certificate Secret in the gateway definition. cert-manager can issue it: ```yaml apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1 kind: Certificate metadata: name: models-tls namespace: infrastructure spec: secretName: models-tls dnsNames: - models.example.com issuerRef: name: letsencrypt kind: ClusterIssuer ``` The cert-manager instance used by KServe webhooks is separate and is configured under `kserve-resources.kserve.certManager`. ## Restricting traffic Model endpoints have no built-in authentication. Protect them with network policy, a service mesh, or an authenticating gateway. ```yaml apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: models-allow-apps namespace: models spec: podSelector: {} policyTypes: - Ingress ingress: - from: - namespaceSelector: matchLabels: kubernetes.io/metadata.name: applications ``` ## Diagnosing access problems | Symptom | Check | --- | --- | Connection refused on port-forward | `kubectl get pods -n models`; the pod may not be ready | `404` on a model path | Confirm the model name in the URL and in `/v1/models` | `503` from the gateway | Workload not ready, or the route points at the wrong service | DNS name does not resolve | Verify the gateway address and external DNS records | Works in-cluster, not externally | Inspect gateway, HTTPRoute, and load balancer state | ```sh kubectl get inferenceservice -n models -o wide kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models -o wide kubectl get httproute -n models -o yaml kubectl describe gateway -n infrastructure shared-gateway ```

67.title: Security
67.content: # Security ## Never commit credentials `hfSecret.token` and any storage credentials belong outside version control. ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve \ -f values.yaml \ --set-string hfSecret.token="$HF_TOKEN" ``` Or keep secrets in a separate, ignored file: ```sh # .gitignore secrets.yaml ``` ```sh helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \ --namespace kserve -f values.yaml -f secrets.yaml ``` > [!CAUTION] > Values supplied to Helm are stored in the release Secret. Anyone who can read Secrets in the release namespace can read a token passed through `hfSecret.token`. Prefer externally managed Secrets. ## Externally managed Secrets ```yaml hfSecret: enabled: true managed: false name: hf-secret ``` The chart references the Secret without creating or reading it, which works with Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, and Vault injection. External Secrets Operator example: ```yaml apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1 kind: ExternalSecret metadata: name: hf-secret namespace: models spec: secretStoreRef: name: vault kind: ClusterSecretStore target: name: hf-secret data: - secretKey: HF_TOKEN remoteRef: key: ml/huggingface property: token ``` ## Service accounts The chart creates one ServiceAccount in the workload namespace: ```yaml serviceAccount: enabled: true name: hf-sa ``` Disable it and supply your own when your platform manages identities: ```yaml serviceAccount: enabled: false models: - name: fraud-detector storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3 serviceAccountName: platform-managed-sa ``` A single ServiceAccount carries all credentials a workload needs. If a model reads from S3 **and** Hugging Face, attach both Secrets to that one account: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: combined-sa namespace: models secrets: - name: s3-credentials - name: hf-secret imagePullSecrets: - name: registry-credentials ``` ## Cloud identity instead of static keys Prefer workload identity over long-lived keys. IRSA on EKS: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: s3-sa namespace: models annotations: eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/model-reader ``` Workload Identity on GKE: ```yaml annotations: iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: model-reader@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com ``` Azure Workload Identity: ```yaml labels: azure.workload.identity/use: "true" annotations: azure.workload.identity/client-id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 ``` ## Private image registries ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: vllmserver: image: registry.example.com/mirror/vllm/vllm-openai tag: v0.11.0 imagePullSecrets: - name: registry-credentials ``` Controllers: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: controller: imagePullSecrets: - name: registry-credentials ``` For `llmInferenceServices`, attach the pull secret to the ServiceAccount used in the workload namespace. ## Endpoint authentication Model endpoints do not authenticate callers. Add protection at the network or gateway layer. Restrict which namespaces may call the models: ```yaml apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: models-ingress namespace: models spec: podSelector: {} policyTypes: - Ingress ingress: - from: - namespaceSelector: matchLabels: kubernetes.io/metadata.name: applications ports: - protocol: TCP port: 8080 ``` Limit outbound traffic once models are cached locally: ```yaml spec: policyTypes: - Egress egress: - to: - namespaceSelector: matchLabels: kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system ports: - protocol: UDP port: 53 ``` > [!WARNING] > Egress restrictions block model downloads from Hugging Face. Apply them only with pre-cached models, a PVC source, or an internal mirror. ## Pod security Upstream runtimes set restrictive container security contexts by default, including no privilege escalation and dropped capabilities. Review before relaxing: ```sh kubectl get clusterservingruntime kserve-huggingfaceserver -o yaml | grep -A12 securityContext ``` The chart's OpenVINO runtime runs as a non-root user with all capabilities dropped. Namespaces enforcing Pod Security Standards may need the `restricted` profile relaxed for GPU workloads that require device access: ```sh kubectl label namespace models pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline ``` ## Multi-tenancy Separate teams with namespaces: ```yaml namespace: models models: - name: team-a-model namespace: team-a storageUri: s3://team-a/model serviceAccountName: team-a-sa - name: team-b-model namespace: team-b storageUri: s3://team-b/model serviceAccountName: team-b-sa ``` Each namespace needs its own ServiceAccount and Secrets. Combine with network policy and resource quotas: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ResourceQuota metadata: name: team-a-gpu namespace: team-a spec: hard: requests.nvidia.com/gpu: "4" ``` ## Supply chain - Pin image tags; avoid `latest` in production, including `llmDefaults.image`. - Pin the chart version when installing from the registry. - Keep `Chart.lock` committed so dependency digests are reproducible. - Mirror upstream images into a registry you control and scan them. ## Review checklist ```sh # No plaintext tokens in tracked files git grep -nE 'hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}' # Confirm which Secrets exist in the workload namespace kubectl get secret -n models # Confirm no unexpected mutable tags helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -f values.yaml | grep 'image:' | sort -u ```

68.title: Serving runtimes
68.content: # Serving runtimes A **ClusterServingRuntime** is a cluster-scoped template that says which container image serves a model format. Entries in `models` select one by name. `llmInferenceServices` entries do **not** use runtimes. They define their container directly. See [LLM inference services](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/llm-inference-services/). ## Runtimes installed by default With default values the chart installs 16 cluster-scoped runtimes: 14 from upstream KServe and 2 added by this chart. | Runtime name | Serves | Typical hardware | Source | --- | --- | --- | --- | `kserve-openvino` | OpenVINO IR, ONNX, TensorFlow, Hugging Face text generation | CPU | This chart | `kserve-vllm-cpu` | Hugging Face causal LLMs | CPU | This chart | `kserve-vllmserver` | Hugging Face causal LLMs | GPU | Upstream | `kserve-huggingfaceserver` | Hugging Face transformers, encoders, embeddings, generation | CPU or GPU | Upstream | `kserve-huggingfaceserver-multinode` | Large Hugging Face models across nodes | Multi-GPU | Upstream | `kserve-tritonserver` | TensorRT, ONNX, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Python backends | CPU or GPU | Upstream | `kserve-tensorflow-serving` | TensorFlow SavedModel | CPU or GPU | Upstream | `kserve-torchserve` | PyTorch `.mar` archives | CPU or GPU | Upstream | `kserve-sklearnserver` | scikit-learn (`joblib`, `pickle`) | CPU | Upstream | `kserve-xgbserver` | XGBoost | CPU | Upstream | `kserve-lgbserver` | LightGBM | CPU | Upstream | `kserve-pmmlserver` | PMML | CPU | Upstream | `kserve-paddleserver` | PaddlePaddle | CPU | Upstream | `kserve-autogluonserver` | AutoGluon | CPU | Upstream | `kserve-mlserver` | Seldon MLServer: scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, MLflow | CPU | Upstream | `kserve-predictiveserver` | KServe predictive server | CPU | Upstream | List them in a live cluster: ```sh kubectl get clusterservingruntime ``` Inspect exactly which model formats a runtime advertises, including versions and priorities: ```sh kubectl get clusterservingruntime kserve-huggingfaceserver -o yaml ``` > [!TIP] > The authoritative list of supported `modelFormat` values is always the live cluster object. Use the command above rather than assuming a format is supported. ## Choosing a runtime ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Model artifact] --> B{Generative LLM?} B -- Yes --> C{GPU available?} C -- Yes --> D[kserve-vllmserveror llmInferenceServices] C -- No --> E[kserve-vllm-cpuor kserve-openvino] B -- No --> F{Framework} F -- scikit-learn --> G[kserve-sklearnserver] F -- XGBoost --> H[kserve-xgbserver] F -- LightGBM --> I[kserve-lgbserver] F -- PyTorch --> J[kserve-torchserve] F -- TensorFlow --> K[kserve-tensorflow-serving] F -- ONNX / TensorRT --> L[kserve-tritonserveror kserve-openvino] F -- Transformers --> M[kserve-huggingfaceserver] ``` ## Selecting a runtime for a model ```yaml models: - name: fraud-detector runtime: kserve-sklearnserver modelFormat: sklearn storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3 ``` If you omit `runtime`, `modelDefaults.runtime` applies. If you omit `modelFormat`, `modelDefaults.modelFormat` applies. > [!IMPORTANT] > `runtime` and `modelFormat` must be compatible. A runtime rejects a format it does not advertise, and the `InferenceService` stays unready with a runtime resolution error. ## Enabling and disabling built-in runtimes Upstream runtimes are controlled per runtime under `kserve-runtime-configs`. Note the key is `disabled`, not `enabled`. ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: enabled: true tritonserver: disabled: true torchserve: disabled: true paddleserver: disabled: true ``` Disable every upstream runtime at once: ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: enabled: false ``` Available runtime keys: `tensorflow`, `mlserver`, `sklearnserver`, `xgbserver`, `huggingfaceserver`, `huggingfaceserver_multinode`, `tritonserver`, `pmmlserver`, `predictiveserver`, `paddleserver`, `lgbserver`, `torchserve`, `autogluonserver`, `vllmserver` ## Overriding runtime images Useful for private registries, air-gapped clusters, and version pinning. ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: huggingfaceserver: image: registry.example.com/mirror/kserve/huggingfaceserver tag: v0.20.0 imagePullSecrets: - name: registry-credentials vllmserver: image: registry.example.com/mirror/vllm/vllm-openai tag: v0.11.0 ``` ## The chart's CPU runtimes ### OpenVINO Efficient CPU inference for OpenVINO IR, ONNX, and TensorFlow models, and the default for `modelDefaults.runtime`. ```yaml clusterServingRuntimes: openVINO: enabled: true name: kserve-openvino image: openvino/model_server:2026.3 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: requests: cpu: "2" memory: 4Gi limits: cpu: "4" memory: 8Gi ``` The `resources` here are the runtime template defaults. Per-model `resources` override them. ### vLLM on CPU Generative inference without a GPU. Use it for development, tests, and small models. ```yaml clusterServingRuntimes: vllmCPU: enabled: true name: kserve-vllm-cpu image: public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-cpu-release-repo:v0.26.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent maxModelLen: 8192 gpuMemoryUtilization: "0.7" shmSize: 2Gi ``` | Key | Meaning | --- | --- | `maxModelLen` | Maximum context length, passed as `--max-model-len` | `gpuMemoryUtilization` | Passed as `--gpu-memory-utilization`; vLLM requires it even in CPU mode | `shmSize` | Size of the `/dev/shm` volume; raise it if vLLM reports shared memory errors | > [!WARNING] > CPU generation is slow. Expect seconds per token for multi-billion-parameter models. Use small models on CPU and reserve large models for GPU. Disable either runtime when you do not need it: ```yaml clusterServingRuntimes: openVINO: enabled: false vllmCPU: enabled: false ``` ## Adding your own runtime The chart does not template arbitrary runtimes. Apply a custom `ClusterServingRuntime` separately and reference it by name: ```yaml apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1 kind: ClusterServingRuntime metadata: name: my-custom-runtime spec: supportedModelFormats: - name: my-format autoSelect: true containers: - name: kserve-container image: registry.example.com/my-runtime:1.0.0 args: - --model_path=/mnt/models ``` ```yaml models: - name: custom-model runtime: my-custom-runtime modelFormat: my-format storageUri: s3://models/custom/v1 ```

69.title: Storage URIs
69.content: # Storage URIs `storageUri` in `models` and `model.uri` in `llmInferenceServices` accept several schemes. The storage initializer downloads the artifact and mounts it at `/mnt/models`. ## Supported schemes | Scheme | Example | Credentials | --- | --- | --- | `hf://` | `hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` | `HF_TOKEN` for gated or private repositories | `s3://` | `s3://bucket/models/fraud/v3` | Secret annotated for S3, attached to the ServiceAccount | `gs://` | `gs://bucket/models/fraud/v3` | Google service account key or Workload Identity | `https://` | `https://example.com/model.joblib` | None, or a public URL | `pvc://` | `pvc://model-store/fraud/v3` | None; the PVC must exist in the workload namespace | `oci://` | `oci://registry.example.com/models/fraud:v3` | Image pull secret | ## Hugging Face See [Hugging Face](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/huggingface/) for tokens, gated repositories, and mirrors. ```yaml models: - name: embeddings runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ``` ## S3 and S3-compatible storage Create a Secret with the storage annotation, then attach it to the ServiceAccount used by the predictor. ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: s3-credentials namespace: models annotations: serving.kserve.io/s3-endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com serving.kserve.io/s3-usehttps: "1" serving.kserve.io/s3-region: eu-west-1 type: Opaque stringData: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: "replace-me" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: "replace-me" --- apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: s3-sa namespace: models secrets: - name: s3-credentials ``` Reference that ServiceAccount: ```yaml models: - name: fraud-detector runtime: kserve-sklearnserver modelFormat: sklearn storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3 serviceAccountName: s3-sa ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > Setting `serviceAccountName` replaces the chart's `hf-sa`. If the same workload also needs Hugging Face access, attach both Secrets to that one ServiceAccount. MinIO and other S3-compatible systems use the same annotations: ```yaml annotations: serving.kserve.io/s3-endpoint: minio.storage.svc.cluster.local:9000 serving.kserve.io/s3-usehttps: "0" ``` Cluster-wide S3 defaults can be set once: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: storage: s3: endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com region: eu-west-1 useHttps: "1" ``` ## Google Cloud Storage ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: gcs-credentials namespace: models type: Opaque stringData: gcloud-application-credentials.json: | {"type": "service_account", "project_id": "replace-me"} --- apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: gcs-sa namespace: models secrets: - name: gcs-credentials ``` ```yaml models: - name: demand-forecast runtime: kserve-xgbserver modelFormat: xgboost storageUri: gs://models/demand/v7 serviceAccountName: gcs-sa ``` ## Persistent volume claims Best for large models reused by many workloads and for air-gapped clusters. ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: name: model-store namespace: models spec: accessModes: - ReadOnlyMany resources: requests: storage: 500Gi ``` ```yaml models: - name: cached-llm runtime: kserve-vllmserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: pvc://model-store/llama-3.1-8b ``` The path after the claim name is the directory inside the volume. Use `ReadWriteMany` or `ReadOnlyMany` so several pods can mount it. Populate the volume with a one-off job: ```yaml apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: Job metadata: name: seed-model-store namespace: models spec: template: spec: restartPolicy: Never containers: - name: seed image: python:3.11-slim command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"] args: - | pip install --no-cache-dir huggingface_hub python -c " from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download snapshot_download('meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct', local_dir='/mnt/store/llama-3.1-8b') " env: - name: HF_TOKEN valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: hf-secret key: HF_TOKEN volumeMounts: - name: store mountPath: /mnt/store volumes: - name: store persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: model-store ``` ## OCI registries Models packaged as OCI artifacts, sometimes called modelcars. ```yaml models: - name: packaged-model runtime: kserve-sklearnserver modelFormat: sklearn storageUri: oci://registry.example.com/models/fraud:v3 ``` Modelcar behavior is configured upstream: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: storage: enableModelcar: true uidModelcar: 1010 ``` Private registries need an image pull secret on the ServiceAccount: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: oci-sa namespace: models imagePullSecrets: - name: registry-credentials ``` ## HTTPS Single-file artifacts served over HTTP or HTTPS: ```yaml models: - name: simple-model runtime: kserve-sklearnserver modelFormat: sklearn storageUri: https://models.example.com/fraud/v3/model.joblib ``` Custom certificate authorities: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: storage: caBundleConfigMapName: custom-ca-bundle caBundleVolumeMountPath: /etc/ssl/custom-certs ``` ## Choosing a scheme ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Where is the model?] --> B{Public Hugging Face model?} B -- Yes --> C[hf://] B -- No --> D{Cluster has internet?} D -- No --> E[pvc:// or s3:// mirror] D -- Yes --> F{Already in object storage?} F -- Yes --> G[s3:// or gs://] F -- No --> H{Reused by many pods?} H -- Yes --> I[pvc://] H -- No --> J[oci:// or https://] ```

70.title: Troubleshooting
70.content: # Troubleshooting ## First commands ```sh kubectl get inferenceservice -n models kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models kubectl get pods -n models kubectl describe pod -n models | sed -n '/Events/,$p' kubectl get events -n models --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -30 ``` Model pods have several containers. Inspect the right one: ```sh kubectl logs -n models -c storage-initializer # download phase kubectl logs -n models -c kserve-container # runtime kubectl logs -n models -c queue-proxy # request handling, when present ``` ## Helm install and template failures | Message | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | `additional properties ... not allowed` | Unknown top-level key | Check spelling; upstream keys go under dependency roots | `found in Chart.yaml, but missing in charts/` | Dependencies not built | Run `helm dependency build` | `cannot re-use a name that is still in use` | Release exists | `helm upgrade` instead, or choose another name | `no matches for kind "InferenceService"` | CRDs missing | Enable the CRD components or install them first | `rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists` | Another release owns the object | Remove the old KServe installation or disable overlapping components | Validate values against the schema without a cluster: ```sh helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -f values.yaml > /dev/null ``` ## A setting has no effect Two frequent causes: 1. **Upstream values at the wrong root.** Helm does not forward parent values into subcharts. ```yaml # Ignored kserve: controller: gateway: ingressGateway: className: contour # Correct kserve-resources: kserve: controller: gateway: ingressGateway: className: contour ``` 2. **A field the chart does not render.** `models` entries support the fields in [Inference services](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/inference-services/) and `llmInferenceServices` entries those in [LLM inference services](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/llm-inference-services/). A key outside those lists is accepted by the schema but ignored by the template. 3. **An explicit `containers` block.** Setting `containers` under `template`, `worker`, or `prefill.template` replaces the generated container for that pool, so `image`, `args`, `resources`, and automatic `HF_TOKEN` injection no longer apply there. Confirm what was actually produced: ```sh helm get manifest model-serving -n kserve | grep -A30 'kind: InferenceService' ``` ## Pod stays in `Init` The storage initializer is still downloading. ```sh kubectl logs -n models -c storage-initializer -f ``` | Message | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | `401` / `403` | Token missing or license not accepted | See [Hugging Face](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/huggingface/) | `404` | Wrong URI | Verify the `hf://org/repo` or bucket path | Slow progress | Large model | Expected; consider [Local model cache](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/local-model-cache/) | `no such host` | Egress blocked or DNS failure | Check network policy and DNS | `AccessDenied` | Storage credentials wrong | Verify Secret and ServiceAccount | ## Pod stays `Pending` ```sh kubectl describe pod -n models | sed -n '/Events/,$p' ``` | Message | Fix | --- | --- | `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` | Free GPUs, add nodes, or lower the request | `Insufficient memory` | Lower `resources.requests` or add capacity | `untolerated taint` | Add tolerations; see [GPU and scheduling](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/gpu-and-scheduling/) | `pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims` | Create the PVC or fix the storage class | ## `CrashLoopBackOff` ```sh kubectl logs -n models -c kserve-container --previous --tail=100 ``` | Cause | Signal | Fix | --- | --- | --- | GPU out of memory | `CUDA out of memory` | Lower `--max-model-len` or `--gpu-memory-utilization`; use a larger GPU | Host out of memory | Exit code 137, `OOMKilled` | Raise `resources.limits.memory` | Shared memory too small | `Bus error`, shm failures | Raise `shmSize` or `devShm.sizeLimit` | Bad arguments | `unrecognized arguments` | Check `args` against the runtime's flags | Wrong format | Model loader errors | Match `modelFormat` to the artifact | Missing GPU driver | `no CUDA-capable device` | Verify the device plugin on the node | ## `CreateContainerConfigError` Almost always a missing Secret or key. ```sh kubectl get secret hf-secret -n models kubectl get secret hf-secret -n models -o jsonpath='{.data.HF_TOKEN}' | head -c 8 ``` The key must be exactly `HF_TOKEN`, and the Secret must exist in the **workload** namespace, not the release namespace. ## `READY` is `False` but pods run ```sh kubectl describe inferenceservice -n models ``` | Condition | Meaning | Fix | --- | --- | --- | `RuntimeNotRecognized` | Runtime name wrong or disabled | `kubectl get clusterservingruntime` | `NoSupportingRuntime` | Format not advertised by any runtime | Set `runtime` and `modelFormat` explicitly | `PredictorConfigurationError` | Invalid predictor spec | Review rendered manifest | Ingress not ready | Gateway missing | See [Networking and endpoints](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/networking-and-endpoints/) | Check the runtime's advertised formats: ```sh kubectl get clusterservingruntime kserve-sklearnserver -o jsonpath='{.spec.supportedModelFormats}' | jq ``` ## Requests fail | Status | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | --- | Connection refused | Pod not ready | `kubectl get pods -n models` | `404` | Wrong path or model name | `curl /v1/models` to list names | `503` | Backend unavailable | Check readiness and route targets | `400` | Payload shape wrong | Match the runtime's protocol | Timeout | Model still loading, or request too large | Watch logs; raise client timeout | ## Webhook errors ``` Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "inferenceservice.kserve-webhook-server.validator" ``` ```sh kubectl get pods -n kserve kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration | grep kserve kubectl get certificate -n kserve kubectl logs -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager --tail=100 ``` Causes include the controller not running, cert-manager not installed, or an expired webhook certificate. ## Controller not starting ```sh kubectl describe pod -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager kubectl logs -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager --tail=200 ``` | Cause | Fix | --- | --- | cert-manager missing | Install cert-manager, then upgrade | Shared resources missing | Ensure one chart sets `createSharedResources: true` | RBAC conflicts | Remove leftovers from a previous KServe installation | Image pull failure | Add pull secrets or mirror the image | ## Duplicate or conflicting resources ```sh helm list -A | grep -i kserve kubectl get crd | grep kserve.io kubectl get clusterservingruntime ``` Two releases installing KServe will fight over cluster-scoped objects. Keep one owner; see [Components](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/components/). ## Collecting diagnostics ```sh NS=models kubectl get all -n $NS > diag-resources.txt kubectl describe inferenceservice -n $NS > diag-isvc.txt kubectl describe llminferenceservice -n $NS > diag-llmisvc.txt kubectl get events -n $NS --sort-by=.lastTimestamp > diag-events.txt kubectl logs -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager --tail=500 > diag-controller.txt helm get values model-serving -n kserve > diag-values.yaml ``` > [!CAUTION] > `helm get values` can include a token supplied through `hfSecret.token`. Remove secrets before sharing diagnostics.

71.title: Upgrades and maintenance
71.content: # Upgrades and maintenance ## Chart versus KServe versions | Field | Meaning | --- | --- | `version` in `Chart.yaml` | Version of this chart; increment for every change | `appVersion` in `Chart.yaml` | KServe version this chart installs | `Chart.lock` | Resolved digests for the seven pinned dependencies | ## Routine upgrade ```sh helm dependency build helm-charts/model-serving helm upgrade model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -n kserve -f values.yaml ``` Preview first on shared clusters: ```sh helm diff upgrade model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -n kserve -f values.yaml ``` Without the diff plugin: ```sh helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -n kserve -f values.yaml > new.yaml helm get manifest model-serving -n kserve > current.yaml diff current.yaml new.yaml ``` ## Upgrading KServe All seven dependencies move together. Mixing versions is unsupported. 1. Edit `Chart.yaml`: set every dependency `version` and `appVersion` to the new KServe version. 2. Refresh the lock and validate: ```sh helm dependency update helm-charts/model-serving helm dependency build helm-charts/model-serving helm lint helm-charts/model-serving --strict helm unittest helm-charts/model-serving ``` 3. Render and inspect the diff, paying attention to CRD changes. 4. Commit `Chart.lock` together with `Chart.yaml`. > [!IMPORTANT] > Helm never upgrades CRDs that already exist. A KServe upgrade adding CRD fields requires applying the new CRDs manually. ```sh helm pull oci://ghcr.io/kserve/charts/kserve-crd --version v0.21.0 --untar --untardir /tmp kubectl apply -f /tmp/kserve-crd/crds/ ``` Verify after upgrading: ```sh kubectl get pods -n kserve kubectl get inferenceservice -A kubectl get llminferenceservice -A kubectl get clusterservingruntime ``` ## Updating model images Runtime images are independent of the KServe version. ```yaml kserve-runtime-configs: kserve: servingruntime: vllmserver: image: vllm/vllm-openai tag: v0.11.0 ``` ```yaml llmDefaults: image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 ``` ```yaml clusterServingRuntimes: vllmCPU: image: public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-cpu-release-repo:v0.26.0 openVINO: image: openvino/model_server:2026.3 ``` Changing a runtime image restarts every model using that runtime. Roll out during a maintenance window, or stage the change with a separate runtime name. ## Updating a single model Point the entry at a new artifact and upgrade: ```yaml models: - name: fraud-detector storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v4 ``` For a zero-downtime swap, run both versions and move traffic afterwards: ```yaml models: - name: fraud-detector-v3 storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3 - name: fraud-detector-v4 storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v4 ``` ## Rollback ```sh helm history model-serving -n kserve helm rollback model-serving 3 -n kserve ``` > [!CAUTION] > Rollback does not revert CRDs. If the failed upgrade applied new CRDs, re-apply the previous CRD version manually. ## Publishing chart changes Merges to `main` publish the exact `Chart.yaml` version. Published versions are immutable, so increment the version before merging. | Change | Version bump | --- | --- | Documentation only | Patch | New optional value with a safe default | Minor | Changed default, renamed value, removed value | Major | KServe dependency upgrade | Minor or major, depending on upstream impact | ## Validation before merging ```sh helm dependency build helm-charts/model-serving helm lint helm-charts/model-serving --strict helm unittest helm-charts/model-serving helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving --namespace kserve --include-crds > /dev/null ``` The repository workflow runs these checks on pull requests and publishes on merge. ## Maintenance checklist | Cadence | Task | --- | --- | Monthly | Review upstream KServe releases and security advisories | Monthly | Check runtime image updates for vLLM and OpenVINO | Quarterly | Upgrade KServe in a test cluster first | Quarterly | Re-verify GPU driver and device plugin compatibility | Continuously | Watch model pod restarts and out-of-memory events | ```sh kubectl get pods -n models --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=OOMKilling ```

72.title: Values reference
72.content: # Values reference Every value owned by this chart. Upstream KServe values live under separate roots; see [Components](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/components/). > [!IMPORTANT] > `values.schema.json` rejects unknown top-level keys. If Helm reports an "additional properties" error, the key is either misspelled or belongs under a dependency root such as `kserve-resources`. ## Top-level values | Value | Type | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | --- | `nameOverride` | string | `""` | Overrides the chart name used in labels | `fullnameOverride` | string | `""` | Reserved for future naming overrides | `namespace` | string | `models` | Namespace for all generated model workloads | `commonLabels` | map | `{}` | Labels added to every chart-owned resource | `commonAnnotations` | map | `{}` | Annotations added to the custom ClusterServingRuntimes | `namespace` is the default workload namespace. Individual entries in `models` and `llmInferenceServices` can override it per workload. ## `components` Enables or disables each upstream KServe chart. All seven default to `true`. | Value | Upstream chart | --- | --- | `components.kserveCrd.enabled` | `kserve-crd` | `components.llmisvcCrd.enabled` | `kserve-llmisvc-crd` | `components.localModelCrd.enabled` | `kserve-localmodel-crd` | `components.kserve.enabled` | `kserve-resources` | `components.llmisvc.enabled` | `kserve-llmisvc-resources` | `components.localModel.enabled` | `kserve-localmodel-resources` | `components.runtimeConfigs.enabled` | `kserve-runtime-configs` | Each entry accepts only the `enabled` key. ## `hfSecret` Hugging Face credentials. See [Hugging Face](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/huggingface/). | Value | Type | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | --- | `hfSecret.enabled` | bool | `false` | Injects `HF_TOKEN` into generated workloads | `hfSecret.managed` | bool | `true` | Creates the Secret from `hfSecret.token` | `hfSecret.name` | string | `hf-secret` | Secret name referenced by workloads | `hfSecret.token` | string | `""` | Token value, used only when `managed` is `true` | Set `managed: false` to reference a Secret you create separately. The Secret must contain the key `HF_TOKEN`. ## `serviceAccount` | Value | Type | Default | Purpose | --- | --- | --- | --- | `serviceAccount.enabled` | bool | `true` | Creates the ServiceAccount for predictor pods | `serviceAccount.name` | string | `hf-sa` | Name used by `models` entries | The ServiceAccount is created only in `namespace`. It is referenced by `models` entries, not by `llmInferenceServices`. ## `clusterServingRuntimes` Two extra CPU runtimes this chart adds on top of the upstream runtimes. See [Serving runtimes](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/serving-runtimes/). ### `clusterServingRuntimes.openVINO` | Value | Type | Default | --- | --- | --- | `enabled` | bool | `true` | `name` | string | `kserve-openvino` | `image` | string | `openvino/model_server:2026.3` | `imagePullPolicy` | enum | `IfNotPresent` | `resources` | map | `1` CPU / `2Gi` requests and limits | ### `clusterServingRuntimes.vllmCPU` | Value | Type | Default | --- | --- | --- | `enabled` | bool | `true` | `name` | string | `kserve-vllm-cpu` | `image` | string | `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-cpu-release-repo:v0.26.0` | `imagePullPolicy` | enum | `IfNotPresent` | `maxModelLen` | integer | `4096` | `gpuMemoryUtilization` | string | `"0.7"` | `shmSize` | string | `1Gi` | > [!NOTE] > The `vllmCPU` runtime does not accept a `resources` key. Set compute for each workload in `models[].resources` instead. ## `modelDefaults` and `models` Defaults applied to every entry in `models`, and the workload list itself. See [Inference services](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/inference-services/). | Value | Type | Default | --- | --- | --- | `modelDefaults.runtime` | string | `kserve-openvino` | `modelDefaults.modelFormat` | string | `huggingface` | `modelDefaults.args` | list | `[]` | `modelDefaults.env` | list | `[]` | `modelDefaults.resources` | map | `8` CPU / `32Gi`–`48Gi` | `modelDefaults.nodeSelector` | map | `{}` | `modelDefaults.tolerations` | list | `[]` | `modelDefaults.affinity` | map | `{}` | `modelDefaults.topologySpreadConstraints` | list | `[]` | `modelDefaults.imagePullSecrets` | list | `[]` | `models` | list | `[]` | Each `models` entry requires `name` and `storageUri`. Every `modelDefaults` key can also be set per model, where it replaces the default rather than merging with it. Scheduling, scaling, and pod metadata fields are accepted at both levels and are omitted from the rendered resource when unset: | Group | Keys | --- | --- | Scheduling | `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, `affinity`, `topologySpreadConstraints`, `priorityClassName`, `schedulerName`, `nodeName` | Scaling | `minReplicas`, `maxReplicas`, `scaleTarget`, `scaleMetric`, `scaleMetricType`, `containerConcurrency`, `timeout`, `canaryTrafficPercent`, `deploymentStrategy` | Pod metadata | `labels`, `annotations`, `imagePullSecrets` | Storage | `volumes`, `volumeMounts` | `scaleMetric` is restricted to `cpu`, `memory`, `concurrency`, or `rps`. ## `llmDefaults` and `llmInferenceServices` Defaults and the generative workload list. See [LLM inference services](/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/helm-charts/model-serving/docs/llm-inference-services/). | Value | Type | Default | --- | --- | --- | `llmDefaults.replicas` | integer | `1` | `llmDefaults.image` | string | `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` | `llmDefaults.args` | list | `[--model, /mnt/models]` | `llmDefaults.resources` | map | `16` CPU / `64Gi` limits | `llmDefaults.router` | map | managed `gateway`, `route`, `scheduler` | `llmDefaults.nodeSelector` | map | `{}` | `llmDefaults.tolerations` | list | `[]` | `llmDefaults.affinity` | map | `{}` | `llmDefaults.topologySpreadConstraints` | list | `[]` | `llmDefaults.imagePullSecrets` | list | `[]` | `llmInferenceServices` | list | `[]` | Each `llmInferenceServices` entry requires `name` and `model.uri`. A `prefill` block accepts the same container keys (`image`, `args`, `resources`, `volumeMounts`, `injectHfToken`) and pod fields as the workload, plus its own `replicas`, `parallelism`, `scaling`, `labels`, `annotations`, and `worker`. Unset fields fall back to the entry, then to `llmDefaults`. Pod fields are accepted in `llmDefaults`, on an entry, and under `worker`, `prefill`, and `prefill.worker`, and are omitted when unset: | Group | Keys | --- | --- | Scheduling | `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, `affinity`, `topologySpreadConstraints`, `priorityClassName`, `schedulerName`, `nodeName` | Identity | `serviceAccountName`, `automountServiceAccountToken`, `imagePullSecrets` | Runtime | `runtimeClassName`, `securityContext`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, `restartPolicy` | Storage | `volumes`, `volumeMounts` | Networking | `hostNetwork`, `hostIPC`, `shareProcessNamespace`, `dnsPolicy`, `dnsConfig`, `hostAliases` | Metadata | `labels`, `annotations` | Init | `initContainers` | A worker field resolves in the order `worker` → entry → `llmDefaults`. ## Upstream dependency roots | Root | Upstream chart | --- | --- | `kserve-crd` | CRD chart values | `kserve-llmisvc-crd` | CRD chart values | `kserve-localmodel-crd` | CRD chart values | `kserve-resources` | Core controller, storage, gateway, cert-manager | `kserve-llmisvc-resources` | LLM controller | `kserve-localmodel-resources` | Local model cache controller and agent | `kserve-runtime-configs` | Built-in ClusterServingRuntimes | Example: ```yaml kserve-resources: kserve: controller: image: kserve/kserve-controller tag: v0.20.0 resources: limits: cpu: 200m memory: 500Mi ``` > [!WARNING] > A legacy top-level `kserve:` block is accepted by the schema but is **ignored** by the upstream subcharts. Helm does not forward parent values into subcharts. Always use the dependency roots above. ## Minimal working example ```yaml namespace: models hfSecret: enabled: true managed: true token: "hf_replace_me" models: - name: sentiment runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver modelFormat: huggingface storageUri: hf://distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english ```
